title: Board comment format: write and read back move, claim, release and round
body:
## Summary
Add functions that write and read back Foreman's machine-readable board comments (move, claim, release, round), and rebuild a ticket's claim and round from a list of comment bodies.

## Context
Spec: specs/001-github-board-adapter.md. The spec requires that `get` can rebuild the claim and the round from comments alone. Nothing writes or reads such comments today. `Claim` and `StageName` are defined in `src/types.ts`; `Status` values come from `STATUSES` in the same file.

Format: each comment is one human-readable sentence, then a line `<!-- foreman {json} -->` where the JSON has a `kind` field (`move`, `claim`, `release`, `round`) plus that kind's fields. Example: `<!-- foreman {"kind":"claim","by":"runner-1","stage":"build","at":"2026-11-18T10:00:00.000Z"} -->`.

New module `src/board/comments.ts` exports `formatMove(from, to, reason)`, `formatClaim(claim)`, `formatRelease(reason)`, `formatRound(n)`, `parseComment(body)` (returns the event or `undefined`), and `boardState(bodies: string[])` returning `{ round: number; claim?: Claim }`.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Each of the four format functions produces a comment that `parseComment` reads back with the same fields.
- [ ] `boardState` with no Foreman comments returns round 1 and no claim.
- [ ] In `boardState`, the latest round comment wins, a claim followed by a release gives no claim, and the latest claim wins.
- [ ] Plain comments and malformed markers (bad JSON, unknown kind, unknown stage, invalid date) make `parseComment` return `undefined` and never throw.
- [ ] The project's existing checks pass (tests, type check, lint).

## Test cases
| # | Type | Steps | Expected result |
|---|------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | check | Run `node --test test/comments.test.ts` | All pass, including a round-trip test for each of move, claim, release and round (claim `at` comes back as a Date with the same ISO string) |
| 2 | check | In the same test file, call `boardState(["plain text"])` | Returns `{ round: 1, claim: undefined }` |
| 3 | check | In the same test file, call `boardState` with round 2 then round 3; with a claim then a release; with claim by A then claim by B | Returns round 3; claim `undefined`; claim with `by` equal to B |
| 4 | check | In the same test file, call `parseComment` on `<!-- foreman {not json -->` and on a claim marker with `"stage":"deploy"` | Both return `undefined` and no error is thrown |
| 5 | check | Run `npm run check` | Type check exits 0 and every test passes, the 18 existing ones plus the new ones |

## Dependencies
- none

## Files likely touched
- src/board/comments.ts
- test/comments.test.ts

## Out of scope
No network calls and no GitHub client. No change to the `Ticket` type, `src/board/labels.ts`, `src/ticket.ts` or the ticket template.

title: GitHubBoard: get and list, with unparseable tickets flagged
body:
## Summary
Add a `GitHubBoard` class that implements `get` and `list` of `BoardAdapter` over the GitHub REST API with an injectable `fetch`, and flag tickets whose body does not match the template instead of dropping them.

## Context
Spec: specs/001-github-board-adapter.md. `BoardAdapter` is in `src/board/types.ts` and has no implementation yet. `statusFromLabels` in `src/board/labels.ts` returns `undefined` for zero or two status labels. `parseTicket` in `src/ticket.ts` throws `TicketParseError`. `boardState` from #T1 rebuilds round and claim from comment bodies. The `Ticket` type in `src/types.ts` has no way to mark an unparseable body.

Changes: `Ticket.body` becomes `TicketBody | null` and `Ticket` gains `parseError?: string`. Constructor: `new GitHubBoard({ repo, token, claimTimeoutMin, fetch? })`, defaulting to the global `fetch`. Requests send the same headers as `src/scripts/create-tickets.ts`. The write methods exist only as stubs that throw `Error("not implemented")`; later tickets fill them in. The claim comes from comments alone, not from the claim label.

## Definition of done
- [ ] `get(n)` returns a Ticket with number, title, status, rawBody, parsed body, and round and claim taken from `boardState` over the issue's comments.
- [ ] `get` on an issue with zero or two status labels rejects with a message containing `#<n> has no single status label`.
- [ ] `get` on an issue whose body does not match the template returns `body: null` and a `parseError` holding the parser's message, without throwing.
- [ ] `list()` returns open issues with exactly one status label, skips pull requests and issues without a status label, and follows `Link: rel="next"` pagination; `list({ statuses: ["QA"] })` returns only QA tickets.
- [ ] `list()` includes tickets with unparseable bodies, flagged with `parseError`.
- [ ] A non-2xx response rejects with an error that contains the HTTP status code and never contains the token.
- [ ] The project's existing checks pass (tests, type check, lint).

## Test cases
| # | Type | Steps | Expected result |
|---|------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | check | Run `node --test test/github-board.test.ts`, case: fake issue #5 with labels `["status: qa"]`, a template body with 2 test cases, and a round comment for round 2 | `get(5)` returns status `"QA"`, round 2, `body.testCases.length` 2, `parseError` undefined |
| 2 | check | Same file, case: fake issue #7 with labels `["bug"]` | `get(7)` rejects with a message matching `#7 has no single status label` |
| 3 | check | Same file, case: fake issue with label `status: ready` and body `"hello"` | `get` resolves with `body` null and `parseError` containing `missing headings` |
| 4 | check | Same file, case: page 1 (with a `Link` next header) holds a ready issue, an issue with no status label, and a pull request with a status label; page 2 holds a qa issue | `list()` returns exactly the ready and qa issues; `list({ statuses: ["QA"] })` returns only the qa issue |
| 5 | check | Same file, case: `list()` where one ready issue has body `"hello"` | That issue is in the result with `body` null and `parseError` set |
| 6 | check | Same file, case: fake fetch answers 404, token is `secret-token-123` | Rejection message contains `404` and does not contain `secret-token-123` |
| 7 | check | Same file, case: issue with a claim comment and no release comment, and no claim label | `get` returns `claim.by` equal to the comment's `by` |
| 8 | check | Run `npm run check` | Type check exits 0 and every test passes |

## Dependencies
- #T1

## Files likely touched
- src/board/github.ts
- src/types.ts
- test/github-board.test.ts

## Out of scope
No real create, move, claim, release, setRound or comment logic (stubs only). No closed issues. No change to `src/board/labels.ts`, `src/ticket.ts` or the ticket template. No network calls in tests. No new runtime dependencies, no `gh` CLI.

title: GitHubBoard: create, move, comment and setRound
body:
## Summary
Implement `create`, `move`, `comment` and `setRound` on `GitHubBoard`, so tickets can be created and their status and round changed through labels and comments.

## Context
Spec: specs/001-github-board-adapter.md. `GitHubBoard` from #T2 has these methods as stubs that throw "not implemented". Comment formats come from `src/board/comments.ts` (#T1). Status label names are in `STATUS_LABELS` in `src/board/labels.ts`.

`move` removes every status label present (zero, one or two) and adds the new one, so it also works for recovery. The move comment records the previous status, or `null` when there was none.

## Definition of done
- [ ] `create` posts the title, body and the single status label, and returns a Ticket with that status and round 1.
- [ ] `move` removes every existing status label, adds the new one, keeps other labels, and posts a move comment that `parseComment` reads back with from, to and reason.
- [ ] `setRound(n, round)` posts a round comment, and `get` afterwards returns that round; a round that is not a positive whole number rejects and sends no request.
- [ ] `comment` posts the given body unchanged.
- [ ] The project's existing checks pass (tests, type check, lint).

## Test cases
| # | Type | Steps | Expected result |
|---|------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | check | Run `node --test test/github-board.test.ts`, case: `create({ title: "T", body, status: "Backlog" })` with a recording fake fetch | One POST to `/repos/o/r/issues` with labels `["status: backlog"]`; the result has status `"Backlog"` and round 1 |
| 2 | check | Same file, case: issue with labels `["bug", "status: ready"]`, call `move(3, "QA", "built")` | Requests: DELETE `/repos/o/r/issues/3/labels/status%3A%20ready`, POST labels `["status: qa"]`, POST a comment; no request removes `bug`; `parseComment` on the comment returns from `"Ready"`, to `"QA"`, reason `"built"` |
| 3 | check | Same file, case: `setRound(3, 2)` then `get(3)` with the fake returning the posted comment | `get` returns round 2 |
| 4 | check | Same file, case: `setRound(3, 0)` and `setRound(3, 1.5)` | Both reject and the fake fetch records no requests |
| 5 | check | Same file, case: `comment(3, "hello **world**")` | One POST to `/repos/o/r/issues/3/comments` with body exactly `hello **world**` |
| 6 | check | Run `npm run check` | Type check exits 0 and every test passes |

## Dependencies
- #T2

## Files likely touched
- src/board/github.ts
- test/github-board.test.ts

## Out of scope
`claim` and `release` stay stubs. No validation of the body in `create`. No change to `src/board/labels.ts`, `src/board/types.ts` or `src/scripts/create-tickets.ts`. No network calls in tests.

title: GitHubBoard: claim and release with stale-claim takeover
body:
## Summary
Implement `claim` and `release` on `GitHubBoard`: a claim fails while another fresh claim exists, and a stale claim can be taken over.

## Context
Spec: specs/001-github-board-adapter.md. `GitHubBoard` (#T2, #T3) has `claim` and `release` as stubs. `CLAIM_LABEL` is in `src/board/labels.ts`. `claimTimeoutMin` is already a constructor option (default in `src/config.ts` is 60). This ticket adds an optional `now?: () => Date` constructor option so tests can fix the clock. A claim is fresh when its age is less than `claimTimeoutMin` minutes.

## Definition of done
- [ ] `claim(n, stage, by)` adds the `foreman: claimed` label, posts a claim comment, and returns the Claim with `at` equal to `now()`.
- [ ] `claim` on a ticket with a fresh claim rejects with a message containing `already claimed by <by> for <stage>` and sends no write request.
- [ ] `claim` on a ticket whose claim is stale succeeds and the new claim replaces it.
- [ ] `release(n, reason)` removes the claim label (a 404 on that removal is not an error) and posts a release comment with the reason; `get` afterwards returns no claim.
- [ ] The project's existing checks pass (tests, type check, lint).

## Test cases
| # | Type | Steps | Expected result |
|---|------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | check | Run `node --test test/github-board.test.ts`, case: unclaimed ticket, `now` fixed at 2026-11-18T12:00:00Z, `claim(4, "build", "runner-1")` | POST labels `["foreman: claimed"]` and one claim comment; returns `{ by: "runner-1", stage: "build" }` with `at` 2026-11-18T12:00:00.000Z |
| 2 | check | Same file, case: timeout 60, now 12:00, existing claim by runner-1 for build at 11:30, call `claim(4, "build", "runner-2")` | Rejects with a message containing `already claimed by runner-1 for build`; the fake records no POST, PATCH or DELETE |
| 3 | check | Same file, case: same as 2 but the existing claim is at 10:59 | Resolves with `by` `"runner-2"` |
| 4 | check | Same file, case: `release(4, "agent timed out")` where the label DELETE answers 404, then `get(4)` with the fake returning the posted comments | `release` resolves; the release comment contains `agent timed out`; `get` returns `claim` undefined |
| 5 | check | Run `npm run check` | Type check exits 0 and every test passes |

## Dependencies
- #T3

## Files likely touched
- src/board/github.ts
- test/github-board.test.ts

## Out of scope
No race handling beyond check-then-write (no re-read after claiming). No check of who wrote a comment. No change to `src/board/labels.ts`, `src/config.ts` or the runner. No network calls in tests.

title: Live smoke script for the GitHub board adapter
body:
## Summary
Add a live smoke script that runs `GitHubBoard` against a real repo end to end and cleans up after itself.

## Context
Spec: specs/001-github-board-adapter.md ("How we will know it works"). `GitHubBoard` is complete after #T4. Existing scripts in `src/scripts/` read `FOREMAN_GITHUB_TOKEN` and take `owner/name` as the first argument; this one follows the same pattern. Closing an issue is not part of `BoardAdapter`, so the script closes the issue with one direct PATCH using the same headers.

Steps the script runs: create an issue titled `Foreman smoke test <ISO time>` with a valid template body and status Backlog; move to Ready, then QA; claim as `smoke` for stage `review`; print `get` as JSON; release; set round 2; print `get` as JSON; close the issue.

## Definition of done
- [ ] `npm run smoke:board -- ahmadtharik/foreman` runs every step above, prints both `get` results, closes the issue, and exits 0.
- [ ] Without `FOREMAN_GITHUB_TOKEN` the script exits non-zero before creating anything.
- [ ] The token never appears in the script's output.
- [ ] The project's existing checks pass (tests, type check, lint).

## Test cases
| # | Type | Steps | Expected result |
|---|------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | check | With a valid token set, run `npm run smoke:board -- ahmadtharik/foreman` | Exits 0; the first printed ticket has `"status": "QA"` and `claim.by` `"smoke"`; the second has no `claim` and `"round": 2` |
| 2 | browser | Open the issue URL the script printed on github.com | Issue is Closed, has label `status: qa` and no `foreman: claimed` label, and its comments in order are: move Backlog to Ready, move Ready to QA, claim, release, round 2 |
| 3 | check | Unset `FOREMAN_GITHUB_TOKEN` and run `npm run smoke:board -- ahmadtharik/foreman` | Exits non-zero with `FOREMAN_GITHUB_TOKEN is not set`; no new issue appears on the repo |
| 4 | check | Run test case 1 again and search the output for the token value | The token value does not appear |
| 5 | check | Run `npm run check` | Type check exits 0 and every test passes; the smoke script is not run by `npm test` |

## Dependencies
- #T4

## Files likely touched
- src/scripts/smoke-board.ts
- package.json

## Out of scope
Not added to CI or `npm test`. No `close` method on `BoardAdapter`. No change to `src/board/github.ts`, `src/scripts/create-tickets.ts` or `src/scripts/setup-labels.ts`. No label setup (labels are assumed to exist).
